sentences.text: This is an Intra Court appeal, under Clause 10 of the Letters Patent, challenging the order dated 24.11.2020 passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P.(C) No. 2634 of 2020.
The writ petitioner is the appellant before us.

2. The writ petitioner approached the learned Single Judge by filing the writ petition being W.P.(C)
No. 2634 of 2020 with the grievance that Ranchi Municipal Corporation had directed the respondent No.-7-M/S Peace Mention to construct a road in Ward No.1, under the Ranchi Municipal Corporation.

The road was being constructed to provide access, cutting across the land belonging to the petitioner pertaining to Khata No.73, Khesra/Plot No. 99 (Part), Mauza Bhitha, Thana No. 187, measuring an area of 3.5 kathas out of total area of 69 decimals.
The learned Single Judge disposed of the writ petition directing the petitioner to file a fresh representation before the Circle Officer, Hehal, Ranchi along with supporting documents.
The Circle Officer, Hehal, Ranchi was directed to take a decision within a period of three months.
3. Mr. Manoj Kumar Choubey, learned counsel for the appellant submits that admittedly the land is not a public land and does not belong to the Ranchi Municipal Corporation.
Without acquiring the land, the respondent- Ranchi Municipal Corporation cannot construct a road by themselves or through any agencies over the land.

4. Mr. Prashant Kumar Singh, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent-Ranchi Municipal Corporation submits that there is a serious disputed question of facts, which cannot be decided in the writ application, thus, the Hon'ble Single Judge has correctly passed the aforesaid order.
5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties, gone through the writ petition, memo of appeal and the counter affidavit filed by the respondent-Ranchi Municipal Corporation.

It is a case of the petitioner that the land pertaining to Khata No.73, Khesra/Plot No. 99 (Part), Mauza Bhitha, Thana No. 187, measuring an area of 3.5 kathas out of total area of 69 decimals which is situated in Ward No.1 of Ranchi Municipal Corporation was recorded on the name of Mostt. Mateeran @ Bibi Maniran.
This petitioner is one of the descendant of khatiyani raiyat Mostt. Mateeran @ Bibi Maniran Bibi.
It is an undisputed fact that the respondent-Ranchi Municipal Corporation is constructing a road which is cutting across the land.
6. Though, no counter was filed by the Ranchi Municipal Corporation in the writ application but the same has been filed in the instant Letters Patent Appeal.
In the counter affidavit, they admitted that they have constructed the road.
In the entire counter affidavit, they have not denied the contention of the petitioner that the land belongs to the ancestor of this petitioner and is a private land.
From the counter affidavit, it is clear that the respondent-Ranchi Municipal Corporation is neither claiming the land to be theirs nor calming that the land is a public land.
Thus, it is clear that they are constructing a road over the land, which does not belong to the Ranchi Municipal Corporation nor the same is a public land.
It is also admitted by the parties that the land over which the road is being constructed, has not been acquired.

Since the land over which the road is being constructed neither belongs to the Ranchi Municipal Corporation nor is a public land, without acquiring the aforesaid land from the rightful owner, no road could have been constructed over the same.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bajranga (Dead) by Lrs. Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors. reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 27, has held that the right to property is still a constitutional right under Article 300A of the Constitution of India though not a fundamental right.

entities.text: Bajranga (Dead) by Lrs. Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors. reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 27
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deprivation of the right can only be in accordance with the procedure established by law.

Thus, the provisions of the Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 had to be complied with before depriving a person of the land in this case.

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Admittedly, the land has not been acquired.
Thus, there is a violation of Article 300A of the Constitution of India as the rightful owner has been deprived of his valuable property, without following the procedure of law.

8. It is also an admitted fact that substantive portion of the road has already been constructed,
which is evident from paragraph No.9 of the counter affidavit.

Thus, we direct the Ranchi Municipal Corporation and the State to acquire the land, upon which, the road has been constructed and pay appropriate compensation in terms of the Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 at the earliest, to the rightful owner of the land.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The entire acquisition process should be concluded within a period of three months from today.

9. Thus, the impugned order dated 24.11.2020 passed by the learned Single Judge in WP(C) No.
2634 of 2020 is set aside.
10. Accordingly, L.P.A. No.41 of 2021 is allowed.
11. All pending Interlocutory Applications stand disposed of.
12. No orders as to costs.
Urgent copies as per Rules.

(S.K. Mishra, C.J.) (Ananda Sen, J.) N.A.F.R. Madhav/-
